transcript.en: TUTOR: Thanks for coming along, Nadia and Fergus.
transcript.zh: 谢谢你们过来，纳迪娅、弗格斯。

transcript.en: So this is a chance for you to give us some feedback about different aspects of your course.
transcript.zh: 这是一个机会，让你们就课程的不同方面给我们一些反馈。

transcript.en: What would you like to begin with?
transcript.zh: 你们想从哪里开始说呢？

transcript.en: NADIA: I've enjoyed the sessions on food safety.
transcript.zh: 我很喜欢关于食品安全的那些课。

transcript.en: There was some information there that I found really surprising, although some was stuff I knew already, like the rise in rates of obesity.
transcript.zh: 其中有些信息让我非常惊讶，虽然也有一些是我已经知道的，比如肥胖率上升。

transcript.en: FERGUS: Yeah, that's been in the news a lot.
transcript.zh: 是啊，这个新闻里报道得很多。

transcript.en: But I hadn't realised that unsafe food causes more than 200 different diseases.
transcript.zh: 但我之前没有意识到，不安全的食品会导致两百多种不同的疾病。

transcript.en: NADIA: No, I'd no idea it was that many.
transcript.zh: 是啊，我也不知道竟然有那么多。

transcript.en: And speaking of diseases, I knew resistance to antibiotics is on the increase, but I didn't know why...
transcript.zh: 说到疾病，我知道抗生素耐药性正在增加，但我不知道原因……

transcript.en: FERGUS: …that it's partly because when animals are treated with antibiotics then consumed by humans, the antibiotics get into the food chain.
transcript.zh: ……部分原因是，动物接受抗生素治疗后被人类食用，抗生素就会进入食物链。

transcript.en: I had no idea about that either.
transcript.zh: 这个我以前也完全不知道。

transcript.en: NADIA: Then the sessions provided a lot of information about plastic pollution from food packaging in the ocean, but I think that most of us were already aware of that.
transcript.zh: 然后，那些课还提供了很多关于海洋中食品包装造成塑料污染的信息，但我觉得我们大多数人已经知道这一点了。

transcript.en: FERGUS: Yeah. But I thought we could have done more on how much food is thrown away unnecessarily through fear of it being out of date, that was only mentioned in passing.
transcript.zh: 是的。不过我觉得，关于人们因为担心食物过期而不必要地丢弃大量食物这一点，我们本可以讲得更多一些；那只是顺带提了一下。

transcript.en: TUTOR: OK, I'll bear that in mind.
transcript.zh: 好的，我会记住这一点。

transcript.en: What did you think about the sessions from visiting lecturers, Fergus?
transcript.zh: 弗格斯，你觉得来访讲师的课程怎么样？

transcript.en: FERGUS: For me the most interesting one was about that project to prevent companies giving incorrect information to consumers about food.
transcript.zh: 对我来说，最有意思的是那个防止公司向消费者提供错误食品信息的项目。

transcript.en: TUTOR: Ah, food fraud, yes.
transcript.zh: 啊，食品欺诈，是的。

transcript.en: FERGUS: I thought it was really good to address a problem that's faced by so many different groups – people with special religious rules, as well as vegetarians and vegans.
transcript.zh: 我觉得解决这个问题非常好，因为它影响着很多不同群体，包括有特殊宗教饮食规定的人，以及素食者和纯素食者。

transcript.en: NADIA: And those with allergies.
transcript.zh: 还有过敏人群。

transcript.en: FERGUS: Yeah. And another thing, we've had effective ways of analysing DNA for some time now and these can easily be applied to analysing food.
transcript.zh: 是的。还有一点，我们已经有相当有效的 DNA 分析方法有一段时间了，而且这些方法很容易应用到食品分析中。

transcript.en: But what the researchers succeeded in doing was to ensure that these tests were carried out at different stages in the food's journey from the producer to the consumer.
transcript.zh: 但研究人员成功做到的是，确保这些检测在食品从生产者到消费者的不同流转阶段都得到实施。

transcript.en: NADIA: So they knew that the food actually came from the place it was supposed to, and had the ingredients it was meant to.
transcript.zh: 这样他们就知道食品确实来自它应该来自的地方，并且含有它应该含有的成分。

transcript.en: FERGUS: Exactly. So customers can be confident about what they buy.
transcript.zh: 没错。这样消费者就能对自己购买的东西有信心。

transcript.en: NADIA: And the researchers had a good system for publicising their findings too.
transcript.zh: 研究人员还有一套很好的系统来公布他们的发现。

transcript.en: FERGUS: Well, I thought there were some problems with that, actually.
transcript.zh: 嗯，实际上我觉得那方面有一些问题。

transcript.en: TUTOR: OK. And do you have any recommendations for new topics that we could include in the course? NADIA: Well, I'm interested in how crop yields can be increased without damaging the environment.
transcript.zh: 好的。你们有没有建议，可以推荐一些我们能加入课程的新主题？嗯，我感兴趣的是如何在不破坏环境的情况下提高作物产量。

transcript.en: FERGUS: But we've already done quite a bit on that – but not so much on the seafood industry, where stocks are in danger of being overexploited as a food source unless we can find ways of keeping stocks up.
transcript.zh: 但我们已经在这方面学了不少；不过关于海鲜产业学得不多。在这个领域，如果我们找不到维持资源量的方法，鱼类等资源就有可能因为作为食物来源而被过度开发。

transcript.en: NADIA: Yes, that'd be a good topic.
transcript.zh: 是的，那会是一个不错的主题。

transcript.en: And I'm interested in the idea of a personalised approach to diet, now we have the technology to analyse exactly what individuals need.
transcript.zh: 我还对个性化饮食方案这个想法感兴趣，因为现在我们有技术可以准确分析每个人需要什么。

transcript.en: FERGUS: That sounds more like a medical topic than food science.
transcript.zh: 那听起来更像是医学主题，而不是食品科学。

transcript.en: NADIA: OK. What about sessions on the variety of food and eating habits around the world?
transcript.zh: 好吧。那关于世界各地食物种类和饮食习惯的课程呢？

transcript.en: That's very relevant nowadays.
transcript.zh: 这个现在非常相关。

transcript.en: FERGUS: Yes, I think the whole class would be interested in that.
transcript.zh: 是的，我觉得全班都会对此感兴趣。

transcript.en: NADIA: Then there's technological stuff, things like 3D printing of food and smart packaging.
transcript.zh: 还有技术方面的内容，比如食品 3D 打印和智能包装。

transcript.en: FERGUS: Mmm – maybe too specialist.
transcript.zh: 嗯，也许太专业了。

transcript.en: TUTOR: Now, I'm particularly interested in your project – the one where you developed a new food product.
transcript.zh: 现在，我对你们的项目特别感兴趣，就是你们开发一种新食品的那个项目。

transcript.en: So talk me through the stages… first you had to decide on your initial aim.
transcript.zh: 那你们给我讲讲各个阶段吧……首先，你们必须确定最初的目标。

transcript.en: FERGUS: We decided we wanted to create something people could eat on the go rather than in a restaurant.
transcript.zh: 我们决定想做一种人们可以边走边吃的东西，而不是在餐厅里吃的东西。

transcript.en: NADIA: Yeah so we chose falafel, which was originally a Middle Eastern snack.
transcript.zh: 是的，所以我们选择了 falafel，它原本是一种中东小吃。

transcript.en: FERGUS: We made up our minds about that pretty quickly.
transcript.zh: 我们很快就决定了这一点。

transcript.en: I know some students found it a lot harder to choose, and wasted a lot of time.
transcript.zh: 我知道有些学生觉得选择主题难得多，还浪费了很多时间。

transcript.en: NADIA: Then we had to do the literature review.
transcript.zh: 然后我们必须做文献综述。

transcript.en: We hadn't done one of these before so the handout with advice for the project was very useful here.
transcript.zh: 我们以前没有做过这种综述，所以项目建议讲义在这里非常有用。

transcript.en: FERGUS: Yes, especially the advice on how to present the information.
transcript.zh: 是的，尤其是关于如何呈现信息的建议。

transcript.en: Then product development, actually deciding what we'd use to make the falafel, and for me the interesting thing about that was that we wanted it to be something a bit different from an ordinary falafel.
transcript.zh: 然后是产品开发，也就是实际决定用什么来做 falafel。对我来说，有意思的是我们希望它和普通的 falafel 有点不同。

transcript.en: NADIA: We really made the right choice when we finally decided to use jackfruit, even though it wasn't something that either of us had ever tasted before.
transcript.zh: 当我们最终决定使用 jackfruit 时，确实做出了正确选择，尽管这并不是我们两个人以前尝过的东西。

transcript.en: FERGUS: Yeah, like the name tells you, it's a fruit but actually it's really good in savoury dishes.
transcript.zh: 是啊，就像名字所说的，它是一种水果，但实际上用在咸味菜肴里非常合适。

transcript.en: The product production, working out how to make the falafel, was harder than I expected because I'd never made them before.
transcript.zh: 产品制作，也就是弄清楚如何做这种 falafel，比我预想的更难，因为我以前从没做过。

transcript.en: NADIA: It was mostly trial and error.
transcript.zh: 这基本上就是反复试错。

transcript.en: We started off with the basic recipe and then experimented and when it went wrong…
transcript.zh: 我们从基础配方开始，然后进行实验；当它失败的时候……

transcript.en: FERGUS: …which it did a lot of the time…
transcript.zh: ……而且很多时候确实会失败……

transcript.en: NADIA: …we just moved on and kept adapting it and in the end it turned out fine and we had a lot of fun.
transcript.zh: ……我们就继续往下做，不断调整，最后结果很好，而且我们也玩得很开心。

transcript.en: FERGUS: We did!
transcript.zh: 确实如此！

transcript.en: TUTOR: Thank you. Well, your project was a very good ….
transcript.zh: 谢谢你们。嗯，你们的项目非常好……
